Braveland is a simple, lightweight turn based strategy in the vein of Shining Force and Final Fantasy Tactics.  You play the role of the Commander of a small and motley crew of fighters seeking vengeance against an evil army that sacked your village.
The player starts with a pitchfork-weilding peasant and an archer, and eventuall unlocks 3 more melee fighters, one more archer, and a healer.  The healer is also able to cast magic bolts at enemies at any range.  The player's character doesn't appear in the battle directly but is able to cast attack and status effect spells during battle.  The tactics are generally pretty simple.  The largest force a player may bring into combat is 5 members but because there is cap on the sum of ranks of player units, the later, there is a choice as to whether to bring a lot of fast/low armor units or a smaller number of slow/heavily armored units.  Despite its apparent simplicity, there is just enough depth to keep the game interesting through its campaign.  The campaign isn't terribly long, with a full playthrough on Normal difficulty taking about 4 hours.  Muc longer than this, and there would need to be more depth to keep the game interesting.
The graphics are pleasant, with a hand-drawn motif thant is a bit more sophisticated than the retro-throwback style so many games employ these days.  The colors are bright, animations are smooth, and it is generally fairly clear what to expect from new units -- both friend and foe -- when you first enounter them.  The music is well produced and fits the game's art style to a T, with a somewhat medieval/fantasy feel and a nice mellow overworld theme and battle music that conveys tension but keeps with the smooth and relaxing feel of the rest of the game.
Bottom Line:  That "smooth and relaxing" feel is this game's draw.  It is not a super deep prove-your-mettle-as-a-general battle/war sim.  It's deep enough to be a little engaging but not so involved as to be distressing.  It is a diversion for a few minutes or hours getting away from the hectic and stressful beat of real life or a soothing distraction to pass the time on a bus or in a waiting room where your undivided focus for several hours simply isn't available.

Black Ops III is, unsurpisingly, not very good. I only played the game's multiplayer, because I only had the multiplayer pack because of Humble Monthly's chubby cheeks.
To start off, I've played a good amount of Call of Duty games in my brief existence on this hellish plane of reality that we choose to call Earth. When I was a console peasant, I kind of enjoyed the games, particuarly MW2 and Black Ops. I've played both of these games on PC, and they still hold up a little bit. The games had consistant tone, they had alright map design, they had robust customization systems for classes and a large array of weapons to put in them. The voice acting was decent, in both English and Russian. People will spray♥♥♥♥♥♥all over COD games, and to be honest, there are way better FPS choices on PC. They were good games for their time.
As you might have guessed, Black Ops III does not do this. Let's start with the characters I noticed while playing the multiplayer.
The game has a wide scale of characters, they're all equally stupid. They have voice lines that are horribly acted in the English version, and acted rather nicely in the Russian version. Sometimes the translation is a little odd, but it holds up pretty well, I'd say. The characters have very little personality, which would be reasonable if they weren't individual. This game, much like R6 Seige, brings in a hero system, every operator is equally different and equally inconsequential. Their weapons are one-shot kills, some have little traps, others have lousy abilities. A big part of the game, and in my opinion the best part of the game, is when the matches end. There's a victory scene where the top 3 players on the winning team do emotes, such as the Gangnam Style dance and the infamous "Dab". This brings me to my next part of the review...
This game's tone is all over the place. Your character can get set on fire and scream terribly as their faces melt, and can also go into a dab at the end of a match. Your character can get dismembered by flesh eating nanobugs, crying in absolute pain, all while dressed as a power ranger. The game couldn't really make up its mind on whether to be a wacky fun shooter where everyone has jet packs strapped to them and dance in goofy ways, or to be a sad, melodramatic game where people are dismembered and disfigured by technology.
Tone and interesting character, however, aren't all that makes a game, what about the gameplay. It's not good, it feels really odd, to be frank. 400 hours of CSGO have made me an FPS god when it comes to COD, but I'm not very good at BOIII. The shooter doesn't really make any sense, there isn't really any tactics to it. The game gave players jet packs and wall running, but didn't increase the players movement speed. You're in Exosuits, sure, but you still feel like a regular dude with a jump jet. The guns are boring, the only one's I liked was the Gorgon LMG and the Pump Shotgun, and I didn't use the shotgun very much because I'd get cussed out by other people for using, well, a shotgun. The maps are not made to be played with jetpacks, and it feels really clumpy and misplaced. The maps aren't very well made, at least the ones that come with the game. I'm not spending the money I stole from a homeless man on COD DLC, I'm not 13.

I have 116 hours in game now, and I have just switched to using HOTAS.  (I am using a Thrustmaster T16000M FCS Flight Pack)  I have never used a HOTAS before and this has added a great new dynamic to the game play for me, giving the game a bit more "realism" in flying. (I guess this could be considered "simcade" as it is NOT in depth like a true flight sim where you would need to study a user manual, and flip switches and such to even turn the engine on. It is very straightforward basic "real" controls as far as I can tell. An hour to learn, and we shall see how many more it will take to master.) While the game is arcade-ish and you can fly in either 3rd or first person (switching view on the fly) using a HOTAS can make this very fun game even more enjoyable! (But for a newb like me on the HOTAS, I went from being pretty damn good with the mouse/keyboard, to sucking, (I am having a blast though! That is just the learning curve for the HOTAS) If you are like me, and just getting into flying games, or especially helicopters, I would HIGHLY recommend getting a HOTAS for the higher level of immersion of flying. I put it off for a long time, and while as stated I went from being an excellent player to a crappy one, I feel like my skill will come up, but even a moderately good keybord/mouse user would dominate me right now. Half the fun is just flying though.
One thing you MUST do is create new squadrons. You cannot expect to start the game and play well with the default squadrons! You can create a seemingly infinite number of squadrons (I have about 24 for different strategies and purposes) A squadron is 2-3 Helis based on a points cost system where each tier (first gen helis: gen 1, to modern helis: gen 4) has a different cap on the amount points you can use to create the squadron. You do not have to earn points, but rather it is just a way for the game to balance out players in each tier. So for example tier 4 (modern helis) has a point limit of 550. I could use my points for an attack chopper with missiles and ATGMs and all the bells and whistles.... but it is gonna cost me more than a transport heli. So you have to balance out your armament loadouts and types of helis and special troops for the different tiers of helis (Tiers 1-4), for both the Russians and US. You will spend some time figuring out what works and what does not. You will need to develop multiple squadrons for each tier that do different things such as a squadron with a heavy focus on troops or a heavy focus on attack helis. This allows you to choose a squadron appropriate for the match, as if you play multiplayer it is usually 1 vs 1 due to low player base. If you choose all attack helis, you will not have troops to deploy to capture bases and have no real way to win. If you play with a team, then you could go full on attack mode and not have any troops in your squadron as long as a teammate does. Again, you will have to figure out what helis and loadouts work when and where.
PROS: Decent graphics, HOTAS support, good number of Helis to choose from and many different loadouts for weapons and troops. The player base while small, is very friendly, and will help you out in learning to play well. For a game that is only in version 0.51 (for those of you not so good at math, the game is only half finished) it is very well put together, with only a few minor bugs. The developers are continuously working on the game, patching things, updating things, adding new helis, and just all around making the game even better! You really cannot beat the cost either. I bought the game a while back when it was on like version 0.34 or something, and it was ten bucks. The Steam Summer Sale has it just under ten bucks for an even more developed game than when I bought it several months back. Another good thing about this game is that every heli can be test flown so you do not have to actually go into a battle. As for the different helis, it is not like some games where you have to "unlock" new weapons, or helis. All helis and weapons loadouts are available immediately to the player. (But as stated above you have to use your points wisely to make each squadron of helis.)
CONS: In cockpit view, all helis, Russian or US, all have the same cockpit. No interior, just a windshield overlay. There is not a very large player base at all. (But again, the game is only on version 0.51 and is fun, just needs players!) The coop mode is kind of boring, but the PvP battles are simply awesome! There are no enemy bot helis in single player or coop. This sucks, but hopefully the devs will fix this in the future.

This game doesnt deserve half of the flack that it gets. Its one of the best third person action games out there, with mechanical depth, fun and diverse enemy types, a good atmosphere and nice set pieces. Is it a horror game?  No its not, but this is the natural direction the games and their story have been going since the second game. Just think about it on a game to game basis. It started in a mansion.... then went to a whole city... then overseas.... did you really think you can keep contained isolated terror from something that started in a house and evolved to a wordlwide pandemic? The first one was the only authentic survival horror game, after that they started adding more explosions,more ammo, a bigger arsenal, more randomly unnecessary plot twists,a burning city you must escape, giant monsters chasing you for the entirety of the game, and just all around action. They just threw in moody music and a difficult control scheme and people accepted it as survival horror.  I challenge someone to name one thing that 2 and 3 had that 6 doesnt. Exploding barrels? check, a counter move? check. A big creepy dude stalking you for the whole game? check. An over the top B grade sci fi story? check. Hell, back then it was even a big deal to beat the game fast so that you could run and gun your way through the game! Not to mention people looooved mercenaries back in the day. People essentially WANTED it to be an action game! The entirety of this experience is essentially a resident evil: greatest hits, just with better (albiet more complicated) mechanics, graphics, and co op. Leon is RE2, Jake is RE3. Chris is the mode in those games when you unlocked the unlimited ammo on your weapons and were allowed to go to town. And dont let my time in game fool you. I also had this for xbox360, and ps3. Twice. Most of the game is missing that isolated and alone feel the first 2 (and 4) resi's had, but just that fact alone should NOT be a determining factor to the games quality. I'm gonna start reviewing call of duty games and say "4/10 not scary enough". The game is great. 5 is great. If you really MUST have your mood however, i suggest the revelations series. Not as mechanically good, but definitely has the ambiance thats apparently necessary for a good RE score. All that said, chill the ♥♥♥♥ out with the QTE's capcom

A board/simulation/turn-based 4x style game that gets better with each iteration. I thoroughly enjoyed the original Rebuild and Rebuild 2 on my cheap smartphone, and am loving all the new stuff in Rebuild 3.
The developer took Rebuild 2 and expanded on it in just about every aspect. More intricate survivor-survivor mechanics (you don't want to do missions with your nemesis), a neat set of perks and abilities you can put on your survivors as they gain levels in their ability of choice to make them better, and the addition of NPC factions that will also be trying to survive and thrive in the zombie apocalypse of NW America/SW Canada. There's also a pretty nifty Campaign that is still being worked on, but adds an awesome mode to the otherwise random map/random size of the first 1.
The game is almost 100% stable, I have had 1 or 2 crashes during Beta testing, and the amount of bugs/glitches reduces with every patch (monthly at the minimum, sometimes faster). A lot of these are cosmetic: him instead of her, using the wrong character name for an event, rather than gamebreaking.
A couple minor issues I have (opinions only, nothing majorly wrong):
The UI can be a bit cumbersome, especially lategame when playing on an Epic map.
Not a big fan of the music. I just mute and kick in a playlist sometimes. It's okay, but it can get a bit repetitive.
Playing on larger maps, there is a lot of micromanaging. It comes with the territory though. If you're controlling 30-50 survivors it's simple. When you have 100+ on 30-40 missions at one time, the message feedback and need to scroll continuously can get wearying.
.... that's really all the negatives I have for it.
If you played 1 and 2, GET 3. GET IT NOW! It's that awesome.
If you are new to the series, I'm not sure what to compare it to in order for you to get a good idea of what it's like. There's a mixture of a dozen different games/genres, all wrapped up in these pretty neat graphics and some dry humor thrown into the bowl. You might try Rebuild 2 on your phone/pad, it's pretty cheap in the various app stores, and see if you like it. If you do, then get this game!
My Score: 9/10 (might go higher once the game is officially out and complete)

The reason it doesn't appeal to me is because this game concentrates more on
than simply plotting down buildings.  There are some buildings and items you can plot down like DLC content, parks, emergency buildings, schools, water and power management, etc.  But skyscrapers, houses and other common buildings you can't pick from a menu and place it.  Most of the building area is managed by zoning off areas (residential, commercial, office, industry).  In other words, depending on how well you run your city will determine how many buildings and homes your city residents build.  If you don't have enough educated people or zoned neighborhoods then businesses will not build up.  If you don't have enough jobs people will move out. I will say that the road customization and mechanics of the game is pretty good.  Some of the DLCs look very impressive but I've not bought them. Thomas Was Alone is the quintessential puzzle-platformer of the decade. It's a perfect marriage of gameplay, storytelling and music. It does everything right from its simple and intuitive controls, music that will give you an eargasm, and a compelling narrative that will leave even the coldest heart weeping uncontrollably.
Visually, the game manages to make striking imagery with simple shapes and lighting that will have you grinning like a star-struck child.
The story, combined with Danny Wallace's narration, is superb. Never had I thought I would be so emotionally invested in a group of geometric shapes, but that's just how fantastic and well-crafted Mike Bithell's writing is.
David Housden's music does what music in a visual medium should do: tell the story audibly. It's gorgeous and never misses a beat.
Thomas Was Alone is a charming, challenging, engaging and utterly terrific game that defies convention, showing how you don't have to make a game that's over 12 hours long with state-of-the-art graphics and a convoluted/poorly written plot. There is beauty in simplicity.
It may be only 3 hours, but could just be the best 3 hours you might ever have with a game.

This is a strategy-RPG game, like a Heroes of Might and Magic. Well, at least regarding the mechanics of the game.
You can buy different kinds of units (melee, ranged, magic) with both basic and special attacks, and you have to fight lots of ennemis on a map with hexagonal cells. Winning a fight will give you money and experience. With the gold, you can buy units and pieces of equipments for your hero : they will boost your entire team and grant them special bonus.
There is a total of 7 different units, and you have a restriction of 5 different units per battle plus no more than 15 stars total (best units are 5 stars, so you can't have 5 different units if you want the best ones).
Your hero have some special powers that can be activated with Fury (not sure about the name in English since I played in French) : you will get this ressource if one of your unit is getting hurt by an ennemy. You can equip up to four pieces of equipment : an armor, a weapon, a hat and a belt.
But sadly, that's it : compared to the same kind of games (HoMM or even King's Bounty), there is nothing more in terms of gameplay. Sure, this game may have been created aiming at specific people, but it looks a little bit too simplified.
Graphics are the kind I like, so that's great for me. But there is not that much content : you have to choose between 3 difficulties at the beginning of the campaign (Easy, Normal, Difficult), and you can adjust it while playing the game (not during a fight, just between them). I did complete the campaign mode firstly on Easy then on Difficult : each time, it took me only 3 hours to defeat the final boss, clearing all of the ennemies on the global map. There's also the Survival mode (you have to survive 10 fights), but that's it.
If you've already played this kind of games, I suggest that you might just go on Difficult mode from the beginning, because it's not even that hard. Moreover, you'll be able to unlock 100% of the achievements within one walkthrough.
To put it in a nutshell, if you are looking for a HoMM-like game that is easy to complete within an afternoon (3 hours for the campaign, no matter which difficulty you choose), I guess that's a fine choice. The current price (4,99€) seems a little bit high, but if you can get it in a bundle, well, it should be okay.

If you like King's Bounty, then you'll like this game because it has most of the same elements.  The main difference is that it automatically subtracts a small fee from the reward for winning a battle to replace units that were lost.  So you only need to head back to buy more units if you are below your leadership cap.  Units have a star ranking, which limits which units you can use together, which is only noticible close to the end of the game with one unit that it effectively prevents you from using.  You could remove two units to make room for this one, but it's not an even trade.  There is also a survival mode, where you have to beat 10 combats in a row, it's not hard to beat, and there is llittle reason to continue playing it once you have beat both modes.  This game was on the short side, but it was fun while it lasted.  If you haven't played King's Bounty, then I suggest getting that first.

The best characteristics of this game are that simplifies , concentrates and executes the Might and Magic and
King's Bounty  formula very well. Turn based combat, with magic on a small / medium grid map.
The game's art is good and overall productions values are correct. The execution of the game overall is good.
What's the problem with the game then?.
Well if you simplify the formula, limiting units,magic and RPG elements to the
minimum extent, you need a lot of content to keep the user playing the game.
On a tablet / mobile environment, the game has more sense than in the PC scenario,even for a casual strategy game (the lack of content is just absurd).
It took me 4.1 hours on normal, to get 90% achievements and to finish the game.
Price tag compared with other games like this, makes the final scenario score even lower.

I've always been particularly fond of Treyarch-made Call of Duty games. They tend to innovate more, guns sound louder and punchier, colors are vibrant. And zombies is always a fun game mode. Black ops 3 is no different in these respects.
The multiplayer is fantastic. I absolutely love the camo system, with constant unlocks for each weapon culminating in several unique challenges (like getting killstreaks with the weapon, getting kills with no attachments/tons of attachments). Completing those nets you a nice looking gold camo. Getting gold camo for all weapons in a class gets you diamond camo for that classes' weapons. And getting diamond for all weapons gets a fantastic looking dark matter. It's constantly rewarding and encourages using all types of weapons. I absolutely fell in love with the Sheiva and Drakon, weapons I would likely not have tried if it weren't for camo challenges.
Plus attachments are great. The thermal scope is particular is one of the best in any COD game. Plus earning new reticles gives even more incentive to using certain scopes. Just tons of customization altogether.
I wasn't a fan of the movement system in Advanced Warfare. Too much zipping, dashing around. It made hitting your target annoying, and ruined the core gameplay in my opinion. Black ops 3 is more restrained, but still different from previous call of duty games, with a simple, controllable double jump and wall running. The maps are tailored for that. It's similar to Titanfall (which has the best movement system of any FPS in my opinion), and it works wonderfully without being overkill.
The maps look great and colorful, and offer plenty of variety. There's only 1 or 2 which I don't love. Unfortunately, Treyarch has made several weapons (and most new ones) only available in loot boxes, which are completely randomly based. They have made challenges that make receiving these easier. I eventually got gold knucles, the FFAR assault rifle, and another melee weapon. I don't love the system, but thankfully the weapons in these crates aren't overpowered. I would much prefer these DLC weapons available under specific challenges.
Weapon balance is great as well. It's been constantly tailored, but they hit a nice spot in my opinion.
And zombies is fantastic. Unfortunately you only get 1 map without the DLC. I enjoy it a lot, but sometimes its a bit too demanding to get pack a punch and other things if you just want a quicker game. DLC helps a lot, with The Giant being perfect for shorter games. Der Eisendrache is probably my favorite map in the series, with fantastic wonder weapons and challenges.
It's not a perfect game, but I absolutely love it. One of my favorite Call of Duty games quite honestly. Black Ops and Black Ops 2 were fantastic, and Treyarch continues the tradition, even if lootboxes are a bit of a pain and annoyance.
I think the fact that this game is still very popular ON PC is a large testament to how great it is. Advanced Warfare died on PC pretty quickly, while this game still routinely is more popular than even the newly released Infinite Warfare.

I came into TOMB RAIDER with pretty high expectations after hearing about what a great game it was... and dear Lord was I mistaken.
Never, and I mean NEVER, have I played a game that felt so unpolished, so.. incomplete... even Sniper Elite V2 was better than THIS, and I hate Sniper Elite V2.
Taking into mind that this is an old game, I  must say it was most likely a genre changing, ground-breaker of a game when it arrived on shelves, but it did not age well. The controls feel more like something out of an old arcade machine, and not the good ones. I mean one of those untouched, unheard of fighting games with about ten buttons for punching and kicking each, and some of the worst receptivity you'll ever play with. I was literally saving every platform I jump I made, and that is preettty bad when most of this game's puzzles involve platforming. You have to hit and hold three buttons at a time to jump and latch onto a platform, and if you do not hit those buttons at exactly the same time, then you either jump incorrectly or don't latch on, and this... oh this is bad. This should be fixed, she should automatically latch on when you jump, or atleast jump in the direction you move. Surely they had the technology to do this at that point in time, right?  Then even worse is her BASIC movement. Yes, Lara's basic steps and turns are so bad it makes some of the game almost unplayable. When she steps forward she moves about 3-5 feet, and when she moves back she does this annoying hop that goes about 5 feet back. This becomes even more nerve-racking when you take into consideration that ANY type of movement left or righ can result in a rol, cartwheel, or side-jump that messes you up 80 percent of the time. This breaks most of the game (at least for me), and makes it darn near almost unplayable.
Then there is the fighting/shooting and obtaining/activating items. This is not as bad as platforming, but pretty close in it's own rite. To pick up on item, you have to face it, stand directly in front of it and press "use". This sounds easy, until you take into mind she moves about 5 feet every step she makes, making this beyond tedious. Then when you must activate an item such as a lever, they want it to be almost exactly on point, and this is more of a pain because most items you must activate are small and hard to get Lara to stand in front of, which makes overall interaction with your enviornment annoying and a pain. The when you shoot, there is a horrid auto-aim mechanic that just makes her swing in circles over and over when enemies move, and she generally stays locked on, so when that enemy is dead, you can bet she'll stil lbe standing there shooting it's dead body. This is somewhat humorous... but a pain in the butt. Generally you are being attacked by 2 or more enemies, so shooting the dead body just ends up getting you killed, and her reflexes are horrible, so turning usually results in more attacks from your enemies, and a dead Lara. This is very tedious, and I do not know how the developers left it like this, and just makes me think  even more that this game is cheap and half-way done.
To end, the game has no soundtrack. Yep, none. The only thing you hear is a looped boom and crumble-like sound that just makes the pretty repetitous and bland enviornments even more so. This not only adds to the overall boredome this game provides, but makes it very annoying to play, and I am thankful the developers at least added the option to turn it off.
Overall, this could have been AMAZING... but because of bad aging and horrible PC controls, it is a horrid train-wreck of an excuse for a "game". The only really good factor is it's saving mechanism, considering it actually functions quite well and is quite fast. Overall i'd give this a 3/10, considering the amount of happiness you fel when you actually get the games mechanics down to a point. For anyone other than die-hard TOMB RAIDERS, i'd say stay away from this game at all costs.

Great game, but in the current state I can't say that I recommend it.
Pros:
-Most playable heroes are really interesting. My favorite is the Raider, who is just a big sweaty man who flails his giant axe around in a manner that can confuse and disorient your opponents. I also enjoyed playing as the Berserker, who is a viking who is less sweaty and has smaller axes, but can deal massive damage if you successfully juke an enemy. You can argue that some are less interesting though, like the flimsy Shinobi or over-nerfed Warlord.
-The game gets really, really intense at some times. I usually play against a friend and we always freak out when we're both at 1 hit away and we're trying to be super offensive as defensive heroes.
-The game looks amazing, and I love the customization options we have for most heroes. My favorite map to look at is Forest, just because of that view off the cliff.
-The unreleased "Tribute," gamemode looks really badass and I cant wait to try it. Can't make promises since it hasn't been released, so you can take this pro with a grain of salt.
-As long as you dont play as Centurion or Gladiator, the community is rather supportive and nice, if you start out with a good first impression to those you are matched with. A lot of people give the community crap but just act nice and you should get nice responses.
Neutral:
-Learning curve is pretty intense. Only buy if you know you'll devote a good amount of time into the game, if you aren't sure just go and either put a few minutes in from a friend who owns the game or watch some gameplay videos, although the latter isn't recommended as much.
-Connection issues are present, but people exaggerate them most of the time. It's probably just as bad as Rainbow Six's connection, imo.
-It has a story mode, but it's pretty bare bones and only used to learn the mechanics of the game and certain characters. I mostly did it to get steel, the currency, though.
-Faction war is present but at times it just feels like you arent fighting for anything because you just barely tip the 50/50 scale when it comes down to just one singular area.
-One hit kills are a thing. Which I personally like in the 4v4 gamemodes, but some others would say otherwise. Basically throwing an enemy off a cliff, or a shorter ledge and then pouncing on top of them, is a one hit kill. If you play for duels, you will not be knocked off an edge most of the time. Ubi recently removed some of these killspots, also.
-Pretty cool halloween event, even though it's temporary. I would put this in positive, but the event is only temporary so it won't apply forever. Introduction to mask outfits were cool, although the masks don't fit well on some heroes such as a conqueror without a rimmed helmet. I think the best part of the event was just all the normal soldiers turning into skeletons because it's just hilarious. Also watching skeletons do the things normal soldiers would do is funny, especially on sentinel when one skeleton gives a short inspirational speech to a group of skeletons. The only thing really wrong with the event is how much each item costs. Masks cost 15,000 and the werewolf emote costs 10,000, which is insane because hiring season 2 or 3 hero costs 15,000. If you didn't stockpile your money before, you might have an issue getting these items.
Cons:
-HUGE HUGE HUGE balancing issues. Let me just number and list things that should be reworked or removed or literally anything to fix
1. Gladiator. Need I say more? Glad has a good size of a stamina pool, a huge health pool for an assassin, a ton of unblockable openers, and a gutstab with too much of a reward. Also not many people seem to realize this but he can get a free gutstab from a deflect. Ubi nerf pls. Glad can, however, have his gutstab parried extremely easily and sidestep light attacks can be punished with a free guardbreak. A smart gladiator would throw these attacks out much less, though.
2. Heroes with incredibly fast zones/attacks in general. After someone uses this for the past 6 times like most of the people who put them to use do, it becomes sort of predictable, but if you aren't playing against the moron who thinks "wow this is super fast, may as well make it my only attack," then they'll start mixing in other extraordinarily fast attacks, such as Warden. I'll get to more about him later. At later levels, this becomes less of an issue as your reaction time has improved, but I had a huge problem with this in early levels.
3. Warden. The community refers to his only purpose as "vortexing." Basically, Warden can do a shoulderbash which will stun enemies so he can get 2 garunteed light attacks, which is about 1 bar of health. Why is this bad? Warden's shoulderbash can be immediatley cancelled into a guardbreak, garunteeing either those 2 lights to continue that shoulderbash chain train or a heavy attack. Also, shoulderbash can be feinted into having an enemy try to dodge-attack counter, just to be parried. Aside from the shoulderbash, Warden has a top heavy that deals massive damage and has a super long range, super fast top lights, and a super fast zone.
4. Berserker is severely underpowered against defensive hereoes such as Conquerer. Simply because Berserker does not have any unblockables, forcing dodges or parries. No one ever goes for parries when out of stamina or at full stamina with a defensive hero. Maybe a Lawbringer will once or twice, but most go for the free shove after a block.
Whatever. Done with the balancing. On to the next problem.
-Ubi won't fix what needs to be fixed. Aka Glad being out for 6 weeks now and still being overpowered and spammy. Highlander still merely dents armor with his giant claymore. I feel like the Shugoki's health gain on a backbreak is sort of weird-ish, but the move is pretty ok other than that. Atleast they gave Centurion a nerf after people discovered he could feint heavy attacks more than 10 times.
[NOTE]: (announced in the a latter patch, the Centurion is getting a HUGE nerf. His punches will no longer be able to stun on walls. Also, they are making the Shinobi less squishy. This may be the start of this con being completely irrelevant.)
-You get currency at a pretty slow rate. Not the biggest problem. Probably the smallest.
I'm just going to wrap up here. If you really feel like picking the game up, go ahead. I'm not leaving For Honor, and I still play it. I just am leaving a negative review in hopes that Ubi does something to fix primarily the balancing issues. Also, if you pick the game up, don't play as Gladiator. No one likes a Glad main.

SUAD он же Shut Up And Dig - это достаточно сложный 2D роглайк платформер от отечественных разработчиков, вышедший в раннем доступе Steam. Базовая часть проекта, по сути, завершена. Основная механика игрового процесса создана, осталось добавить больше разновидностей уровней, чем разработчики в данный момент и заняты. Игра получилась отличной, если не брать в учёт кое-какие недостатки, которые, возможно, являются как таковыми лично для меня.
Что же такого нам предлагает Shut Up And Dig? Классическое управление платформера и огромные уровни, генерируемые при каждом новом прохождении. Главный герой игры – это милая маленькая эльфийка с розовыми волосами, но пусть её внешность вас не обманет, она очень умело владеет киркой и может её использовать не по назначению. Вы можете избирать путь так, как пожелаете. Хотите копать в левую сторону, чувствуя, что там вас ждёт нечто ценное? Ваше право, а может, хотите вниз, вправо или вверх? Пожалуйста! Только будьте осторожны, шахты наполнены различными ловушками и монстрами, которые с радостью помогут распрощаться с жизнью неаккуратному шахтёру. Кроме голодных врагов и смертоносных ловушек, в шахтах вы можете найти различные предметы, которые помогут вам в прохождении, пока вы не допустите хотя бы одну ошибку - игра не прощает ошибок.
На данный момент, в игре готов один мир, который рассчитан примерно на 10 часов игрового процесса. Автор обещает нам пять различных рандомно генерирующихся типа мира на релизе игры, и, примерно десять секретных мини-миров, каждый из которых имеет своих уникальных противников, игровой процесс и саундтрек. На данный момент игра выглядит очень мрачно и гнетуще, в хорошем смысле. Стиль у SUAD очень привлекательный, спрайты персонажей, противников и мира гармонично сочетаются. Саундтрек и общая звуковая составляющая на уровне, но ничего особенного и запоминающегося вы здесь не услышите.
Игра действительно очень сложная, как и по геймплею так и по освоению в целом. Для того чтобы понять как всё здесь работает, придётся потратить несколько часов, это точно. Множество различных предметов, противников, особенностей и не понятная на первый взгляд система крафта заставят вас с непониманием смотреть в монитор и думать «А что же это такое и зачем это здесь вообще?». Управление в игре, мягко говоря, неудобное. Игра не имеет толкового туториала, нет, она его, конечно, имеет, но после его завершения, лично я ничего не понял и не усвоил, может быть это я такой, не знаю. В отзывах в Steam многие жалуются на неудобное и непонятное управление, возможно, в этом что-то есть?
Разработчики активно занимаются игрой, пытаясь добавить в неё новые особенности: персонажи, эффекты, предметы, а так же исправляют баги. Если всё то, что обещано добавят, в игре можно будет с удовольствием провести несколько десятков часов. В данный момент контента в игре мало, но он качественный. Играть приятно и интересно, неудобное управление не считается.
В целом, игра хорошая, если вы любите сложность в игровом процессе, в данном случае – хардкор. Действительно, всё очень и очень сложно, казуалы – мимо сразу. Главным достоинством проекта является полная нелинейность игрового процесса, каждое прохождение – уникально и зависит не только от вас, но и от фортуны. Стоит ли в неё играть? Скорее да, чем нет.

Crysis 2 is an extremely interesting game that deviates slightly from your generic out the box FPS. Instead of placing you in the boots of a generic off-the-shelf character, with a sci fi protaganist who comes across as an extremely powerful super soldier who also is granted limited sympathy, something most shooters these days lack. Alcatraz is sent in with a squad of marines to investigate an infection in New York. Being effectively killed with the rest of the squad, he is rescued by Prophet from the previous game who sacrifices himself and bequeathes the Nanosuit to Alcatraz.
This leads an extremely compelling sci fi story through New York with alien invasions, corporate sabotage and some killer environments. Crysis 2 truly has the most stunning city scapes in gaming and it's only recommended for high end PCs. The gameplay is also engaging and adds diversity to a standard shooter formula with invisibility, increased strength, bulletproof armour and tactical options.
However the game isn't without its bugs and occasionally annoying AI, especially the Ceph. This is par for the course in FPS these days and it usually doesn't detract from the games fun.

As someone who's cleared all 4 "souls like" games from From Software, the difficulty of this game was just right. Bosses felt challenging but except for the final boss (which took me maybe 5ish tries) the other 4 went down on the first or second attempt. Other veterans beware if you like your longer games. Howlongtobeat states that people average at a little under 8 hours to beat the main story, but steam says I took 4 (I was probably close to 5). There is a New Game+ that limits your health to 2 down from 5 (and some enemies/attacks deal 2 damage) as well as a boss rush, though.
One thing I did find irritating is that, because you don't really have an invulnerability period, sometimes you'll get stunlocked to death. One enemy might knock you down, during which you can only wait to get back up, but another enemy or two will attack you even while still down and most likely kill you. There's nothing that I know of that you can do in these situations.
Aside from that, I was surprised in how the game lets you tackle any of the first three (of four) areas/bosses in order and how similar in difficulty they felt even though I gained experience over time. That said, the first I've done happened to give a rather overpowered weapon.
Wonderful game, definitely worth buying.

I've always been particularly fond of Treyarch-made Call of Duty games. They tend to innovate more, guns sound louder and punchier, colors are vibrant. And zombies is always a fun game mode. Black ops 3 is no different in these respects.
The multiplayer is fantastic. I absolutely love the camo system, with constant unlocks for each weapon culminating in several unique challenges (like getting killstreaks with the weapon, getting kills with no attachments/tons of attachments). Completing those nets you a nice looking gold camo. Getting gold camo for all weapons in a class gets you diamond camo for that classes' weapons. And getting diamond for all weapons gets a fantastic looking dark matter. It's constantly rewarding and encourages using all types of weapons. I absolutely fell in love with the Sheiva and Drakon, weapons I would likely not have tried if it weren't for camo challenges.
Plus attachments are great. The thermal scope is particular is one of the best in any COD game. Plus earning new reticles gives even more incentive to using certain scopes. Just tons of customization altogether.
I wasn't a fan of the movement system in Advanced Warfare. Too much zipping, dashing around. It made hitting your target annoying, and ruined the core gameplay in my opinion. Black ops 3 is more restrained, but still different from previous call of duty games, with a simple, controllable double jump and wall running. The maps are tailored for that. It's similar to Titanfall (which has the best movement system of any FPS in my opinion), and it works wonderfully without being overkill.
The maps look great and colorful, and offer plenty of variety. There's only 1 or 2 which I don't love. Unfortunately, Treyarch has made several weapons (and most new ones) only available in loot boxes, which are completely randomly based. They have made challenges that make receiving these easier. I eventually got gold knucles, the FFAR assault rifle, and another melee weapon. I don't love the system, but thankfully the weapons in these crates aren't overpowered. I would much prefer these DLC weapons available under specific challenges.
Weapon balance is great as well. It's been constantly tailored, but they hit a nice spot in my opinion.
And zombies is fantastic. Unfortunately you only get 1 map without the DLC. I enjoy it a lot, but sometimes its a bit too demanding to get pack a punch and other things if you just want a quicker game. DLC helps a lot, with The Giant being perfect for shorter games. Der Eisendrache is probably my favorite map in the series, with fantastic wonder weapons and challenges.
It's not a perfect game, but I absolutely love it. One of my favorite Call of Duty games quite honestly. Black Ops and Black Ops 2 were fantastic, and Treyarch continues the tradition, even if lootboxes are a bit of a pain and annoyance.
I think the fact that this game is still very popular ON PC is a large testament to how great it is. Advanced Warfare died on PC pretty quickly, while this game still routinely is more popular than even the newly released Infinite Warfare.

Tomb Raider I simply put... is a classic.
The main focus in TRI are puzzle solving, platforming, and explorations with a a little action in between. It's all about the tombs! Unlike the sequels, the original is pretty basic. The effect pays off well allowing the player to experience plently of memorable moments right down to a T-REX in a lost valley all the way to an alien ooze fest in Atlantis. Cool!
The improvements in TR2-5 are mostly cosmetic and never did they drastically stray away from the formula TRI established. And why should they have? Master those controls and you'll understand why these earlier TR installments were a blast to play.

Tomb Raider I is a very interesting game to say the least. It has aged rather well but is clearly from the time period, and it sits strongly embedded in those roots from the level design right down to the controls. Lara herself controls like a tank. A very agile tank but still a tank. She moves slow, turns on a dime (if that dime was abnormally obese and the size of a small car) and her jumps respond about as quickly as a sloth. The controls and response times do take some getting used to because of this but once you get them the platforming becomes incredibly easier. This is good considering the gameplay itself is about 70-80 percent platforming with the remaining percent being loading from deaths and shooting it out with enemies. Although the platforming is very well done (once you get the controls down) the same can't exactly be said about the gunplay. It may not be the main focus, that belongs to the tomb raiding, it is certainly a big part and definitely the weakest area of the game. All fights boil down to "hold fire and jump while moving to the side or back." Now this shouldn't normally be a problem but due to the way the jump works (there is a delay by roughly half a second to a second from when you press it so the game knows how you want to jump i.e. forward, backward, standing, or sideways) it makes many fights frustrating when you accidentally jump straight up instead of to the side or back or vice-versa when you are close to ledges and jump off. That still also gets much easier as the game goes on and you get a better grasp on the controls and when you do the already mundane fights become chores to do as all that's left is to jump and hold fire until the enemy is dead. Aside from that I will say this game impressed me greatly with the variety of animations and the art direction though the locales were definitely generic Seriously!? 2 Areas?! You get a tomb in a mountain and 2 tombs in the same desert?!
CAUTION SPOILER:
Hell the third tomb was a boat ride away from the second in atlantis in a pyramid in a mine on an island in a lake in the desert??
/SPOILER
Even though there are few larger locales many levels do have smaller areas with each feeling diverse and unique. The level design is lacking in some places though and you may have to consult a guide as  there are times the levels don't lead you anywhere at all and where you have to go isn't obvious. Also the game breaks its own rules from time to time. Overall a very enjoyable game. Get it if you enjoy older games or platformers with hard traps.

The original classic from 1996 is back!
Tomb Raider is a game that needs no introduction. Starring one of the first mainstream female characters in video gaming history, and featuring gameplay designed around a Indiana-Jones style of adventuring. This is the original classic of one of my most cherished franchises in gaming history.
Every level is cleverly designed to make you explore and the emphasis is on puzzles more then combat. The atmosphere in this game is perhaps it's most unique feature. There isn't much music, but a lot of ambient background noise that will keep you unsettled as you explore the tombs of ancient civilizations.
One disappointment with this PC release is that much of the music from the Playstation release has been removed, which is a bit of a let down. This game is also hit or miss how well it will perform on modern PC's. The game is emulated using Dosbox and it may not always run correctly on modern graphics cards/sound cards without graphical glitches or sound glitches.
If you can look past it's dated graphics, old-school grid-based controls, and it's clunky (but creative) puzzle logic then Tomb Raider is a classic game that I highly recommend to any fan of Action/Adventure games.

Great game, but in the current state I can't say that I recommend it.
Pros:
-Most playable heroes are really interesting. My favorite is the Raider, who is just a big sweaty man who flails his giant axe around in a manner that can confuse and disorient your opponents. I also enjoyed playing as the Berserker, who is a viking who is less sweaty and has smaller axes, but can deal massive damage if you successfully juke an enemy. You can argue that some are less interesting though, like the flimsy Shinobi or over-nerfed Warlord.
-The game gets really, really intense at some times. I usually play against a friend and we always freak out when we're both at 1 hit away and we're trying to be super offensive as defensive heroes.
-The game looks amazing, and I love the customization options we have for most heroes. My favorite map to look at is Forest, just because of that view off the cliff.
-The unreleased "Tribute," gamemode looks really badass and I cant wait to try it. Can't make promises since it hasn't been released, so you can take this pro with a grain of salt.
-As long as you dont play as Centurion or Gladiator, the community is rather supportive and nice, if you start out with a good first impression to those you are matched with. A lot of people give the community crap but just act nice and you should get nice responses.
Neutral:
-Learning curve is pretty intense. Only buy if you know you'll devote a good amount of time into the game, if you aren't sure just go and either put a few minutes in from a friend who owns the game or watch some gameplay videos, although the latter isn't recommended as much.
-Connection issues are present, but people exaggerate them most of the time. It's probably just as bad as Rainbow Six's connection, imo.
-It has a story mode, but it's pretty bare bones and only used to learn the mechanics of the game and certain characters. I mostly did it to get steel, the currency, though.
-Faction war is present but at times it just feels like you arent fighting for anything because you just barely tip the 50/50 scale when it comes down to just one singular area.
-One hit kills are a thing. Which I personally like in the 4v4 gamemodes, but some others would say otherwise. Basically throwing an enemy off a cliff, or a shorter ledge and then pouncing on top of them, is a one hit kill. If you play for duels, you will not be knocked off an edge most of the time. Ubi recently removed some of these killspots, also.
-Pretty cool halloween event, even though it's temporary. I would put this in positive, but the event is only temporary so it won't apply forever. Introduction to mask outfits were cool, although the masks don't fit well on some heroes such as a conqueror without a rimmed helmet. I think the best part of the event was just all the normal soldiers turning into skeletons because it's just hilarious. Also watching skeletons do the things normal soldiers would do is funny, especially on sentinel when one skeleton gives a short inspirational speech to a group of skeletons. The only thing really wrong with the event is how much each item costs. Masks cost 15,000 and the werewolf emote costs 10,000, which is insane because hiring season 2 or 3 hero costs 15,000. If you didn't stockpile your money before, you might have an issue getting these items.
Cons:
-HUGE HUGE HUGE balancing issues. Let me just number and list things that should be reworked or removed or literally anything to fix
1. Gladiator. Need I say more? Glad has a good size of a stamina pool, a huge health pool for an assassin, a ton of unblockable openers, and a gutstab with too much of a reward. Also not many people seem to realize this but he can get a free gutstab from a deflect. Ubi nerf pls. Glad can, however, have his gutstab parried extremely easily and sidestep light attacks can be punished with a free guardbreak. A smart gladiator would throw these attacks out much less, though.
2. Heroes with incredibly fast zones/attacks in general. After someone uses this for the past 6 times like most of the people who put them to use do, it becomes sort of predictable, but if you aren't playing against the moron who thinks "wow this is super fast, may as well make it my only attack," then they'll start mixing in other extraordinarily fast attacks, such as Warden. I'll get to more about him later. At later levels, this becomes less of an issue as your reaction time has improved, but I had a huge problem with this in early levels.
3. Warden. The community refers to his only purpose as "vortexing." Basically, Warden can do a shoulderbash which will stun enemies so he can get 2 garunteed light attacks, which is about 1 bar of health. Why is this bad? Warden's shoulderbash can be immediatley cancelled into a guardbreak, garunteeing either those 2 lights to continue that shoulderbash chain train or a heavy attack. Also, shoulderbash can be feinted into having an enemy try to dodge-attack counter, just to be parried. Aside from the shoulderbash, Warden has a top heavy that deals massive damage and has a super long range, super fast top lights, and a super fast zone.
4. Berserker is severely underpowered against defensive hereoes such as Conquerer. Simply because Berserker does not have any unblockables, forcing dodges or parries. No one ever goes for parries when out of stamina or at full stamina with a defensive hero. Maybe a Lawbringer will once or twice, but most go for the free shove after a block.
Whatever. Done with the balancing. On to the next problem.
-Ubi won't fix what needs to be fixed. Aka Glad being out for 6 weeks now and still being overpowered and spammy. Highlander still merely dents armor with his giant claymore. I feel like the Shugoki's health gain on a backbreak is sort of weird-ish, but the move is pretty ok other than that. Atleast they gave Centurion a nerf after people discovered he could feint heavy attacks more than 10 times.
[NOTE]: (announced in the a latter patch, the Centurion is getting a HUGE nerf. His punches will no longer be able to stun on walls. Also, they are making the Shinobi less squishy. This may be the start of this con being completely irrelevant.)
-You get currency at a pretty slow rate. Not the biggest problem. Probably the smallest.
I'm just going to wrap up here. If you really feel like picking the game up, go ahead. I'm not leaving For Honor, and I still play it. I just am leaving a negative review in hopes that Ubi does something to fix primarily the balancing issues. Also, if you pick the game up, don't play as Gladiator. No one likes a Glad main.

With around 45 hours, I feel I have experienced enough of what the game has to offer to say it is a massive dissapointment. The saddest part is there's a good game hidden underneath all of this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t (That's of course to facilitate micro transactions, which I still had content behind despite paying a hundred dollars for the collector's editon.) The combat system is great. In need of some tweaking perhaps, but good. The Idea of Samurai vs Knights vs Vikings is pretty cool, and what drew me to the game in the first place. If it weren't for the awful latency and being probably the only modern muliplayer game without dedicated servers and the reasons I'll get into in a moment, I'd absolutely reccomend it. However in it's current state it's just awful.
Gear is the largest glaring problem that ultimately makes this game suffer outside of the statless 2v2 or 1v1 modes. It's honestly laughable that it's marketed as a compedative 'fighting game/brawler' of sorts. For those familiar with the genre, imagine if you were playing Street Fighter for instance, and after playing a bunch of hours of Ryu you got a headband that doubled the damage of your Haduken move. Top this with matchmaking that goes off of your highest played class and it just destroys any opportunity for you to try anything new. Would I love to play the Shinobi or maybe switch it up and play the Warden class? I sure would, too bad I'm going to get matched as a level 0 with people who have 40+ hours of experience on thier character because my Orochi has as much on it, not even to mention the min/maxed gear they no doubt have. Sure you can play 1v1 or 2v2 but if you have 3 friends who all want to play like me, you're shoehorned into a 4v4 mode with gear and powerups like it's some failed abortion of Mount and Blade and Super Smash Brothers.
Next I'll mention "The community". I have played over a thousand hours of Dota 2, over three hundred of League of Legends, and about 150-200 hours or so of CS:GO. All of these are infamous for having the most try hard, hostile, and angry comminities in the gaming sphere, and I can say without a doubt in my mind that For Honor tops them all by a wide, WIDE, margin. Everyone in this game seems to take the name of the game extremely seriously, and will expect you to conform to a set of arbitrary, made up, and often random rules. Push someone off a cliff to exploit bad positioning? Oh boy get ready for the biggest, angriest temper tantrum in all chat about how you're a "No honor scumbag" even though the devs intended you to have the ability to throw people off of cliffs and into water. In a 2v2, kill your first opponent, and then gang up on the last one to secure a win? Same thing.
I have never met a community in a game who will expect you to intentionally gimp yourself to give your opponent a chance to win. I don't throw this term around lightly, but it's one of the most halariously entitled things I've ever seen. Imagine if in Counter Strike people expected you to not engage in a fire fight against an opponent an insisted on assanine "duels" even in deathmatch mode. Never once have I seen anyone in this game throw out a 'gg' at the end of a game, even sarcastically. The community is (at least I hope) filled with nothing but 13 year olds and manchildren. It's honestly very sad.
Oh, and you need to latch this thing onto a Uplay account, so that's another negative I won't get into too much. The final, crowning embarassment, is what I mentioned in the first paragraph. This game, a game which relies heavily on netcode and split second reactions, timing, and setups runs in Peer to Peer. Why Ubisoft, a multi-million dollar company can't shell  out the cash to pay for some dedicated servers for the game is baffling. And before the Defense Force comes at me, no, Peer to Peer is not better. It's awful, especially for a game like this. It maybe would be acceptable if this were an indie game that was made 6-8 years ago, but these days for a major publisher it's just embarrassing. Oh and it has rediculous DRM that requires you to be constantly connected to Ubisoft's flimsy, unreliable servers to enjoy even the singleplayer.

Was looking for a good game pad flying combat game and tried this on early access. Overall, positive and good balance between simple game play and playable controls. Because it is a helicopter game of course it takes some understanding; with a game pad I was able to get the jist of flying within 15 minutes and from then on I went onto win a game against a computer (without enemy aircraft of course). I like the game mechanics of base capture, dropping off personnel to man or re-inforce the base defenses. It reminded me of an updated 3D Choplifter or Rescue Raiders (if you are old like me, you recognize these names) And the combat I thought was fine. Graphics were quite good and you could feel the difference between the various copters. Overall fun and hit the right level of simplicity vs authentic-feeling mil sim that I wanted.
On the negative side, the UI to actually get into the game could be greatly simplified. I spent maybe 5 minutes trying to figure out how to actually jump in and play and was almost ready to give up before I stuck with it. Also for some reason with game pad  I could not put my cursor on my size of screen; fortunately I could revert to mouse for the interface clicking.
The biggest negative is that I did not find any US servers except one; so I had to content myself to learn the game by myself - though it did help me learn how to fly without someone constantly killing me. I will definitely look for future updates as I content myself with bombarding enemy vehicles and bases while I learn how to fly better.
